P.text: A user's veTRUST lock reaches its natural expiry; the lock-end is <= the epoch-end due to week-rounding; the reward system snapshots userBondedBalanceAtEpochEnd at the exact epochTimestampEnd timestamp.
P.evidence_quote: Every user who lets their lock reach its natural expiry loses 100% of their rewards for the final epoch in which they were bonded. The reward system snapshots `userBondedBalanceAtEpochEnd` at the exact `epochTimestampEnd` timestamp.

I.text: Rewards should be allocated pro rata to users' shares of the total bonded balance, so a user bonded for part or all of an epoch should receive that epoch's rewards.
I.evidence_quote: Contradicts documented design - The NatSpec promises rewards "allocated pro rata to users' shares of the total bonded balance." A user bonded for an entire epoch receiving 0% of their share violates this guarantee.

V.text: Because veTRUST balance decays linearly to zero at lock expiry and the snapshot occurs at epoch-end (>= lock-end), the snapshot returns zero for the epoch in which the lock expires, so the user can never claim that epoch's rewards; users with lock duration <= epochLength can lose 100% of rewards.
V.evidence_quote: As `veTRUST` balance decays linearly to zero at lock expiry, and the lock-end is always <= the epoch-end (due to week-rounding), the snapshot returns *zero* for the *epoch in which the lock expires*. The user was bonded for a part or all of that epoch, yet received nothing.
